question: Which items are off-plan this week, ranked by dollar impact? Show the items.
For item <ID> at org 2012, show planned on-hand vs actual on-hand over the last 8 weeks.
How much stockout risk (below safety stock) is at 2120 right now, and which SKUs make it up?
Which items are unplanned (activity but no plan baseline) at 2012?
Compare plan bias between 2012 and 2120 — are we over- or under-planning?
What should I escalate right now (Tier-3), listed by item?
Which purchase orders should I expedite, and which are chronically-late suppliers to fix instead?
What is the on-hand value by org this week? (do not sum on-hand across weeks)
Which inbound shipments or orders should I cancel or defer because we are already overstocked (above 3x safety stock)?
Which planner should I alert this week — who owns the most newly off-plan dollars?
What mirage or misleading fields should I avoid trusting in this data?
Which items are off-plan this week, ranked by dollar impact?
sql: SELECT item_id, item_description, organization_code, week_start, planned_pab, actual_end_on_hand, onhand_variance_abs, onhand_variance_pct, onhand_variance_dollar, onhand_status FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_plan_vs_actual WHERE week_start = (SELECT MAX(week_start) FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_plan_vs_actual) AND onhand_status IN ('red','yellow') ORDER BY ABS(onhand_variance_dollar) DESC LIMIT 50

question: Show planned on-hand vs actual on-hand for one item at an org over the last 8 weeks.
sql: SELECT item_id, organization_code, week_start, planned_pab AS planned_on_hand, actual_end_on_hand AS actual_on_hand, onhand_variance_abs, onhand_variance_pct, onhand_variance_dollar FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_plan_vs_actual WHERE item_id = '48111850' AND organization_code = '2012' ORDER BY week_start DESC LIMIT 8

question: Which items breached safety stock (actual on-hand below planned safety stock) and how much stockout risk in $?
sql: SELECT item_id, item_description, organization_code, week_start, actual_end_on_hand, planned_safety_stock, ROUND((planned_safety_stock-actual_end_on_hand)*applied_standard_cost,0) AS stockout_risk_usd FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_plan_vs_actual WHERE week_start = (SELECT MAX(week_start) FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_plan_vs_actual) AND planned_safety_stock > 0 AND actual_end_on_hand < planned_safety_stock ORDER BY stockout_risk_usd DESC LIMIT 50

question: How much stockout risk is at 2120 right now, with the SKUs that make it up?
sql: SELECT item_id, item_description, organization_code, week_start, ROUND((planned_safety_stock-actual_end_on_hand)*applied_standard_cost,0) AS stockout_risk_usd FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_plan_vs_actual WHERE organization_code = '2120' AND week_start = (SELECT MAX(week_start) FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_plan_vs_actual) AND planned_safety_stock > 0 AND actual_end_on_hand < planned_safety_stock ORDER BY stockout_risk_usd DESC LIMIT 100

question: Which items are unplanned (activity but no plan baseline)?
sql: SELECT item_id, item_description, organization_code, week_start, actual_end_on_hand, actual_po_received, actual_shipped FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_plan_vs_actual WHERE planned_pab IS NULL AND week_start = (SELECT MAX(week_start) FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_plan_vs_actual) ORDER BY organization_code, item_id LIMIT 100

question: How much did we receive vs plan, and ship vs plan, for one item this week?
sql: SELECT item_id, organization_code, week_start, planned_sales_orders AS planned_ship, actual_shipped, shipped_variance_abs, actual_po_received FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_plan_vs_actual WHERE item_id = '48111850' ORDER BY week_start DESC LIMIT 8

question: Compare plan bias between 2012 and 2120 — are we over- or under-planning?
sql: SELECT org, plan_name, items, item_weeks, avg_overage_pct, pct_green, pct_red, pct_unplanned FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_agg_scorecard ORDER BY org

question: What should I escalate right now (Tier-3), by item?
sql: SELECT item_id, item_description, organization_code, week_start, onhand_variance_pct, onhand_variance_dollar, alert_tier FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_plan_vs_actual WHERE alert_tier = '3 · Escalate' AND week_start = (SELECT MAX(week_start) FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_plan_vs_actual) ORDER BY ABS(onhand_variance_dollar) DESC LIMIT 50

question: Show the exception queue ranked by cost (one row per item), with chronic-supplier flag.
sql: SELECT item_id, item_description, organization_code, exception_type, abs_var_dollar AS dollar_at_risk, onhand_variance_pct, chronic_pct_late, root_flag FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_exceptions WHERE worst_rn = 1 ORDER BY abs_var_dollar DESC LIMIT 100

question: Which purchase orders should I expedite, and which are chronic-supplier problems to fix instead?
sql: SELECT item_ref AS item_id, org AS organization_code, supplier_name, order_ref, slip_days, timing_band, recommended_maneuver, chronic_pct_late, CASE WHEN chronic_pct_late>=60 THEN 'Systemic (fix supplier)' ELSE 'One-off (expedite)' END AS decision FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_order_stage_gold WHERE lane='purchase' AND recommended_maneuver <> 'None' ORDER BY (chronic_pct_late>=60) DESC, slip_days DESC LIMIT 100

question: Which orders are arriving too early — candidates to defer or downsize?
sql: SELECT item_ref AS item_id, org AS organization_code, supplier_name, order_ref, slip_days, timing_band, recommended_maneuver FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_order_stage_gold WHERE timing_band = '0 Very early' ORDER BY slip_days ASC LIMIT 100

question: Which ABC class carries the most variance dollars this week, and the top items in it?
sql: SELECT item_id, item_description, abc, organization_code, week_start, onhand_variance_dollar FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_plan_vs_actual WHERE week_start = (SELECT MAX(week_start) FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_plan_vs_actual) AND abc IS NOT NULL ORDER BY ABS(onhand_variance_dollar) DESC LIMIT 50

question: What is the on-hand value by org this week (point-in-time, never summed across weeks)?
sql: SELECT organization_code, ROUND(SUM(actual_end_on_hand*applied_standard_cost),0) AS onhand_value_usd, COUNT(*) AS items FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_plan_vs_actual WHERE week_start = (SELECT MAX(week_start) FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_plan_vs_actual) GROUP BY organization_code ORDER BY organization_code

question: Which items flipped off-plan since last week (newly red), ranked by new $ exposure?
sql: WITH w AS (SELECT item_id, organization_code, week_start, onhand_status, onhand_variance_dollar, LAG(onhand_status) OVER (PARTITION BY item_bigint_key, org_bigint_key ORDER BY week_start) prev FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_plan_vs_actual) SELECT item_id, organization_code, week_start, ROUND(ABS(onhand_variance_dollar),0) AS new_exposure_usd FROM w WHERE week_start=(SELECT MAX(week_start) FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_plan_vs_actual) AND onhand_status='red' AND COALESCE(prev,'')<>'red' ORDER BY new_exposure_usd DESC LIMIT 100

question: Upstream plant material movements by type and plant (context tier — not summable with DC numbers).
sql: SELECT organization_code AS plant, root_cause AS movement_type, txns, total_qty FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_rootcause_plant ORDER BY total_qty DESC LIMIT 50

question: Which inbound orders should I cancel or defer because the item is already overstocked (>3x safety stock)?
sql: SELECT o.item_ref AS item_id, o.org AS organization_code, o.order_ref, o.supplier_name, o.recommended_maneuver, o.timing_band, p.actual_end_on_hand, p.planned_safety_stock FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_order_stage_gold o JOIN sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_plan_vs_actual p ON o.item_ref = p.item_id AND o.org = p.organization_code WHERE p.week_start = (SELECT MAX(week_start) FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_plan_vs_actual) AND p.planned_safety_stock > 0 AND p.actual_end_on_hand > 3*p.planned_safety_stock AND o.recommended_maneuver LIKE 'Defer%' ORDER BY p.actual_end_on_hand DESC LIMIT 100

question: Which planner should I alert this week — who owns the most newly off-plan dollars?
sql: WITH w AS (SELECT organization_code, planner_name, onhand_status, onhand_variance_dollar, week_start, item_bigint_key, org_bigint_key, LAG(onhand_status) OVER (PARTITION BY item_bigint_key, org_bigint_key ORDER BY week_start) AS prev FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_plan_vs_actual) SELECT COALESCE(planner_name,'Unassigned') AS planner, organization_code, COUNT(*) AS newly_red_items, ROUND(SUM(ABS(onhand_variance_dollar)),0) AS newly_red_dollar FROM w WHERE week_start=(SELECT MAX(week_start) FROM sandbox_operations.po_management.sdp_plan_vs_actual) AND onhand_status='red' AND COALESCE(prev,'')<>'red' GROUP BY COALESCE(planner_name,'Unassigned'), organization_code ORDER BY newly_red_dollar DESC LIMIT 20

content:
PERSONA: You serve Milwaukee Tool supply planners (operational) and planning managers (analytical) for the P1 'Actuals Supply Plan'. Answer in plain business language, then show the records.
ALWAYS SHOW THE RECORDS BEHIND A NUMBER: whenever a question implies a total, count, or $ figure, also return the underlying items that make it up — item_id, item_description, organization_code, week_start — ranked by dollar impact (ABS(onhand_variance_dollar) or the relevant $), typically LIMIT 50-100. Never answer with only a scalar when identifiable rows exist. Echo the filters you applied (org, week, status) so the planner can reproduce it.
GRAIN: sdp_plan_vs_actual is one row per item x organization x week (Monday-start weeks). Every aggregate is a roll-up of these identifiable rows, so a drill-down list always exists.
PLAN VS ACTUAL (the core): planned_pab = planned/projected on-hand; actual_end_on_hand = actual ending on-hand; planned_sales_orders vs actual_shipped = demand plan vs actual; actual_po_received = supply actual. onhand_variance_abs = actual - planned; onhand_variance_pct = 100*(actual-planned)/abs(planned); onhand_variance_dollar = variance x standard cost. Status: green <=15%, yellow 15-30%, red >30% (onhand_status). alert_tier: '1 · Monitor' >15%, '2 · Alert' >30% or >$50K, '3 · Escalate' >50% or >$200K or below safety stock.
NEVER SUM on-hand across weeks: actual_end_on_hand and planned_pab are point-in-time stock levels. For 'on-hand value' use the LATEST week only (MAX(week_start)). Flows (actual_po_received, actual_shipped) ARE additive across weeks; stock is not.
ORG IS A JUDGEMENT CONTEXT, not just a filter. 2012 (Olive Branch) is ~24x larger and ~5x harder to plan than 2120 (Mexico); both OVER-plan (positive bias) — it is NOT 'inverted'. A fixed $200K escalate threshold never fires at 2120. When comparing orgs, use relative terms (%, ratios, percentiles) from sdp_agg_scorecard, not raw $ totals. Org->plan mapping: 2120 -> '20 Mexico Supply Plan', all else -> '20 Global Supply Plan' (already applied in the tables; each org appears on exactly one plan).
UNPLANNED vs NO-ACTUAL: planned_pab IS NULL means 'unplanned (no plan baseline)', not 'no actual'. ~18% of 2012 item-weeks are unplanned vs ~2% at 2120.
EXCEPTIONS: sdp_exceptions holds red/yellow rows with exception_type, abs_var_dollar, and chronic-supplier flag; use worst_rn=1 for one row per item. Rank by dollar, never by unit-miss (a $0.01 part must not top the list).
ORDER TIMING & CHRONIC SUPPLIERS: sdp_order_stage_gold has slip_days, timing_band, recommended_maneuver, chronic_pct_late per order. Preemptive rule: recommend Expedite/Defer/Monitor/Reorder from the band; if chronic_pct_late>=60 it is a SYSTEMIC supplier problem (fix the supplier) rather than a one-off (expedite this order). PO timing comes from the historical lead-time-error source, NOT purchase_receipt_line.expected_receipt_date (which is a same-day mirage).
PLANT TIER: sdp_rootcause_plant covers upstream PLANT orgs (1006-1021), NOT the DCs 2012/2120. It is context only — never add its quantities to DC variance numbers.
SHARED-SKU COMPARISONS: only ~5,717 items exist at both orgs (2120 is ~41% Mexico-exclusive). Cross-org 'same item' comparisons must INNER JOIN on item_id.
HONESTY RULE: if something needs data not in these tables (live 'where is it now' track-and-trace, lat/long mapping, re-promise history), say it is not available yet and offer the closest proxy — do not fabricate. Answer only from these sandbox tables; never from raw prod.
